title: Retained alarm
brief: Program an alarm that remembers a fault even after the original fault signal disappears.
requirements: Fault Detected (I0.0) becomes ON when the machine detects a fault. Acknowledge (I0.1) is the operator's acknowledgement button. Use Alarm Memory (M0.0) to retain the fault state.
Initially, Alarm Memory (M0.0) and Alarm Lamp (Q0.0) must both be OFF.
When Fault Detected (I0.0) switches ON, set Alarm Memory (M0.0) and turn Alarm Lamp (Q0.0) ON.
When Fault Detected switches OFF again, Alarm Memory and Alarm Lamp must remain ON so the fault is not forgotten.
When Acknowledge (I0.1) is ON and Fault Detected is OFF, clear Alarm Memory (M0.0) and switch Alarm Lamp (Q0.0) OFF. The lamp must remain OFF when Acknowledge is released.
If Fault Detected (I0.0) and Acknowledge (I0.1) are ON simultaneously, the fault takes priority: Alarm Memory (M0.0) and Alarm Lamp (Q0.0) must stay ON.
objective: Store a fault and manage acknowledge priority.
hints: A set coil writes TRUE when its rung is true; a reset coil writes FALSE. Otherwise each leaves the bit unchanged.
For fault priority, execute reset first and set second. Then use the memory bit to drive the output.
